note: Attacker-controlled PNG chunk length is parsed from the input stream; this length is later used as the byte count for reading the ancillary chunk payload and drives the streaming buffer reallocation.

The code caches a pointer to ctx->data before reading the chunk payload. This pointer is kept alive across the subsequent chunk read and is later used by ancillary-chunk processing, even though reading the next chunk may reallocate/free ctx->data.

The full ancillary chunk payload is read into ctx->data. In streaming mode, when chunk.length exceeds the current buffer size, read_data() reallocates ctx->data and frees the old buffer that the cached 'data' pointer still references.

Reallocation branch: with streaming enabled and the attacker-chosen chunk length (bytes) greater than the current buffer size, spng__realloc() allocates a new buffer and frees the old one, making the cached 'data' pointer in read_chunks_before_idat stale.
After the reallocation, ctx->data points to the new live buffer into which the attacker-supplied chunk bytes are copied; the caller's cached 'data' pointer refers to the freed old buffer.

sPLT ancillary-chunk processing dereferences the stale 'data' pointer (the buffer freed by the realloc performed during read_chunk_bytes), producing a heap use-after-free read before the first IDAT chunk is reached.
